title: WASSCE Financial Accounting: Complete Preparation
description: A full 10-module WASSCE Financial Accounting preparation course aligned to the WAEC syllabus: bookkeeping fundamentals, cash book & bank reconciliation, financial statements, partnership & company accounts, manufacturing & cost accounting, public sector & non-profit accounting, accounting ethics & ICT, examination practice, revision, and a full mock examination with a Certificate of Completion.
outcomes: Understand the WAEC Financial Accounting exam structure and marking scheme
Apply the accounting equation and double-entry bookkeeping
Prepare cash books and bank reconciliation statements
Prepare trading, profit & loss accounts and the balance sheet with adjustments
Handle partnership, company, manufacturing and cost accounts
Understand public-sector/non-profit accounting, ethics and ICT in accounting
about: This is the complete TIH WASSCE Financial Accounting preparation course, organised into ten modules aligned to the WAEC Financial Accounting syllabus and examination structure (objective and essay/practical).

Every content lesson has a video and printable notes with worked layouts; downloadable resources include ledger templates, journal worksheets and accounting formula sheets. The course ends with a full mock examination and a Certificate of Completion.
Financial Accounting rewards practice — prepare many accounts by hand. Use this course together with the official WAEC syllabus, your teacher’s guidance and WAEC past questions for best results.
requirements: A phone or computer with internet
A spreadsheet (e.g. Excel) for the ICT module (optional)

lessons.title: 3.1 Single Column Cash Book
lessons.html:
WASSCE Financial Accounting · Module 3: Cash Book & Bank ReconciliationWAEC syllabus aligned

Single Column Cash Book

This lesson builds the cash book & bank reconciliation through clear rules, worked examples and timed practice. Watch the video, study the worked example, then complete the two exercises before the short quiz.

Key points

  • Learn the rule/format for Single Column Cash Book and how WAEC tests it in the objective and essay/practical papers.
  • Study a worked layout (proper headings, debit/credit sides, totals) and the marks for method.
  • Practise with past-question-style items under timed conditions, ruling accounts neatly and balancing them.

📥 Guide: Cash Book & Bank Reconciliation

  • Cash book records cash and bank transactions (a book of original entry AND a ledger).
  • Columns: single (cash), double (cash + bank), triple (cash + bank + discount).
  • Petty cash uses the imprest system for small payments.

This lesson builds financial statements through understanding the principle and applying it to WAEC-style accounting questions. Watch the video, study the worked example, then complete the two exercises before the short quiz.

  • Practise with past-question-style items under timed conditions, ruling accounts neatly and balancing them.

📥 Guide: Financial Statements

  • Trading account finds gross profit = sales − cost of goods sold.
  • Profit & loss account finds net profit = gross profit + other income − expenses.
  • Balance sheet (statement of financial position) lists assets, liabilities and capital.
  • Depreciation: straight-line = (cost − residual) ÷ useful life.
  • Adjustments: accruals, prepayments, bad debts and provisions.

lessons.html:

Certificate Requirements

To graduate and earn your TIH WASSCE Financial Accounting Certificate you must:

  • Complete the lessons in Modules 1–9.
  • Complete the practical accounting and examination practice.
  • Pass the module quizzes and the Final Assessment.
  • Pass the final Certificate of Completion assessment.

Use this together with the official WAEC syllabus, a calculator, your teacher’s guidance and WAEC past questions.

questions.question: Accounting is best described as the process of:
options: Recording, classifying, summarising and reporting financial transactions
questions.explanation: Accounting records and reports financial information.

questions.question: The accounting equation is:
questions.explanation: Assets = Capital (Owner’s Equity) + Liabilities.

questions.question: WASSCE Financial Accounting is assessed by:
questions.explanation: It has objective and essay/practical components.

questions.question: In the essay/practical paper you earn marks mainly for:
options: Correct format, method and figures that balance
questions.explanation: Correct layout, method and balanced figures score marks.

questions.question: The "going concern" concept assumes a business will:
options: Continue operating for the foreseeable future
questions.explanation: Going concern assumes continued operation.

questions.question: In double-entry bookkeeping every transaction affects:
options: At least two accounts (a debit and a credit)
questions.explanation: Each transaction has equal debit and credit entries.

questions.question: A trial balance is prepared to:
options: Check that total debits equal total credits
questions.explanation: It checks the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger.

questions.question: A source document for a credit sale is the:
questions.explanation: A sales invoice is the source document for a credit sale.

questions.question: The rule "debit the receiver, credit the giver" applies to:
questions.explanation: It is the rule for personal accounts.

questions.question: A suspense account is used temporarily when:
options: The trial balance does not balance
questions.explanation: A suspense account holds a difference until errors are found.
